limited_overlap.description: applicants with prior_earnings between 56,920 and 941,070: 95% of the 1200 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (1994 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 18,258 against 37,657; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: months_unemployed p=0.068 (-16706, -899, -30966, -69571 dollars per SD); ethnicity p=0.0715 (+10455, +1719, +18567, +40705 dollars per SD); age p=0.0716 (+12444, +102, +23006, +51593 dollars per SD); parttime p=0.0739 (-47210, -2046, -87923, -199518 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
14.0% of training rows have a cross-fitted propensity outside the overlap bounds; the all-rows ATE depends on the outcome model in those rows, and the overlap-bounded estimate is 2,316 dollars.
Instrument check (distance_km, responders only): complier effect 12,238 dollars with 90% interval [2,866, 21,609], against the ATE 2,744. The complier effect and the ATE are different quantities.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 31,656.5 (train) against 26,087.6 (test); months_unemployed 2.7 (train) against 3.2 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 4.9%. 107 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 3,933 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 2.1%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['months_unemployed', 'ethnicity', 'age'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
